$comment: Kiln's install for this frame, as data. Format: docs/design/kiln/frames-as-data.md. A draft (#621): the contract (kiln/apps/kiln/test/contract) reads route, touch and each step's id, writes, reboots, downloads and taps; the engine reads the rest from phase 2. `words`: what Kiln's screens say for this frame (the shared wizard reads them, #621).

releases.why: Glassworks: vX.Y.Z (every release so far) or aqara-s1-plus-vX.Y.Z, and the S1's armeabi-v7a APK

legacy.why: s1.edm.sh, the first installer page, was the S1's: its hash links (/#/wifi) and its release route before #28 (/api/release-asset) lead here

enter.why: Stock software has no adb: FEL is the only way in. The button is under the back cover (recovery.json).

words.name: Aqara S1 Plus
words.photoAlt: The S1 Plus board with the back cover off. The recovery button is circled: right of the shield's notch, below the round sensor window.

fastboot.title: One click to continue.
fastboot.body: The panel restarted into the installer. Nothing has been written yet.

adb.title: One last click.
adb.body: The panel is starting its new software. Leave its screen alone meanwhile.

connect.title: Connect to your panel.
connect.body: It should be running Glassworks and plugged in to this computer. Nothing is reflashed.

drivers.win: Windows needs a driver once: in Zadig, give USB Device (1f3a:efe8) the WinUSB driver.
drivers.linux: Linux needs a udev rule once for 1f3a:efe8 and 1f3a:1010.

factory.title: As it came from Aqara
factory.detail: The original software, then a factory reset on the panel. Everything is removed.
factory.restored: One last step, on the panel: swipe down, tap Settings on the app's notification, then Advanced settings → Factory reset.

keep.title: Keep its settings
keep.detail: Aqara's apps come back first, over USB with the panel running. Wi-Fi and the rest stay.
keep.giving: Giving the panel back to Aqara's apps
keep.stillOn: Aqara's apps are back, but Glassworks is still on.
keep.restored: It is restarting with Aqara's software and apps. Your settings and Wi-Fi are as they were.

on.line: Updates from Home Assistant install with nobody at the panel. The root update service in its boot image installs them.

missing.line: This panel's boot image has no root update service, so each update waits for a tap on the panel. Updates still come from Home Assistant. Install again with Kiln to add it.

unknown.line: Kiln couldn't read the root update service back. Glassworks' Device page on the panel says which it is.
